observation.visible_scene: A high aerial (drone-style) view over a dense autumn forest with mixed green, yellow, orange and red canopies. A long, narrow, irregular blue pond/lagoon sits in the upper-middle ground, bordered by a pale linear strip (runway or cleared corridor) running diagonally to the right. On the right side are buildings: a large white multi-storey structure near the lower-right edge and a pinkish block further up, with a hazy flat horizon and distant development beyond. A tall, soft-edged shadow (bulbous top, elongated body) lies across the right-centre treetops, partially overlapping the lit forest and the white building's left flank.
visible_changes: The scene is essentially static: the pond, the pale corridor, the forest edge, the white and pink buildings, and the hazy horizon hold the same positions relative to the frame from t=0.0 to t=3.2, indicating little or no camera pan/zoom.

The large shadow over the right-centre treetops drifts only marginally (its top bulb and lower body shift a few pixels toward the right / slightly change extent) across the sequence; no other moving objects (vehicles, people, water motion) are discernible.
Tree canopies show no visible wind deformation at this resolution; the water surface appears calm and unchanged.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the slight shadow shift (slow sun/cloud change vs. movement of an off-frame occluder vs. minor camera drift) is not determinable from the excerpt.
What object casts the tall shadow is not visible.
Any motion that begins or ends outside this 3.2-second crop is unknown.
uncertain_details: Whether the small apparent shadow displacement is real translation or sub-pixel/compression noise is uncertain.
The exact direction and magnitude of the shadow's drift are subtle and hard to confirm frame-to-frame.
No clear camera movement is established; the background's fixed framing argues against a pan, but a tiny drift cannot be fully excluded.
